subject: Fenrir3b elevated timeouts — timeline, mitigations, and follow-up
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@brightanalytics.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reed <ops@brightanalytics.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Fenrir3b - increasing 5xx/timeouts since 11/24 (examples + impact)

Hi Markus / Kimberly,

We're seeing a sharp rise in 5xx and request timeouts coming from calls routed to fenrir3b over the last ~24 hours. Error rate went from ~0.2% to ~4.7% across our production traffic between 11/24 22:00 UTC and 11/25 06:00 UTC. The failures are primarily timeouts (upstream 504) with occasional 503s.

Affected endpoints: /generate, /chat/streaming. Impact: user-facing failures in our summarization flows; approx 18% drop in success for requests above 4k tokens. We're on Dedicated with model pin fenrir3b:v2.1.

Sample timestamps (UTC):
- 2026-11-24T22:45Z 504
- 2026-11-24T23:12Z 503
- 2026-11-25T02:03Z 504

I've attached a snippet of our request traces and the gateway logs (fenrir-logs-1124.txt). Can you confirm whether Redwood has active incidents for fenrir3b and expected ETA for a mitigation? We need to inform our PM/ops and decide whether to failover to a different model.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Director, Platform Engineering
Bright Analytics

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@brightanalytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-25T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fenrir3b - increasing 5xx/timeouts since 11/24 (examples + impact)

Hi Elena — thanks for the detailed notes and the log attachment. We see the same signal in our telemetry (elevated queue depth and tail latency for fenrir3b pools in us-west-2).

Initial actions we've taken (immediate):
- Enabled automatic fallback routing for your project to fenrir-lite-v2 for requests over 3k tokens to reduce failure surface.
- Increased request timeout windows temporarily from 30s -> 45s for fenrir3b routes for your account.
- Opened an ops bridge and notified the runtime team; Ben is leading triage.

Can you confirm whether enabling the fallback is acceptable for Bright Analytics for next 24 hours? We'll monitor error rate and CPU/GPU metrics and update regularly.

Attachment: initial-ack.txt (ops bridge id).

— Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Elena Morales <elena@brightanalytics.com>
Cc: Tom Reed <ops@brightanalytics.com>, CloudCo Infra <cloudinfra@cloudco.io>
Date: 2026-11-26T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: Fenrir3b triage update — suspected KV cache memory leak, rollout of rolling restart

Team,

Quick technical update from runtime triage:
- Observed behavior: fenrir3b inference workers in the fenrir-prod-us pool accumulated resident memory over long session windows, leading to blocking GC sweeps and queue buildup. The blocking periods correlate with elevated tail latency and subsequent 5xx responses when request queues hit the circuit breaker threshold.
- Evidence: heap growth traces matched with your gateway traces (thanks Elena) and model-side logs.
- Immediate mitigation applied: we initiated targeted rolling restarts across the fenrir-prod-us pool to drain the worst-off hosts and reduced max concurrent requests per worker from 16 -> 10 to limit queue depth.
- Short-term fix ETA: we pushed a micro-patch to the runtime that adjusts KV cache eviction heuristics and improves backpressure signalling; patch is currently in canary. Full rollout scheduled tonight (2026-11-26 23:30 UTC) with staged verification.

Action items for Bright Analytics:
- Continue to accept fallback to fenrir-lite-v2 for heavy requests for the next 24 hrs (recommended).
- If you prefer, we can programmatically route certain high-impact endpoints to fenrir-lite-v2 only for the duration — let us know the endpoints.

Tracking ticket: INF-4821 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4821).

I'll post telemetry snapshots in the bridge after each stage.

— Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@brightanalytics.com>, Tom Reed <ops@brightanalytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Fenrir3b STATUS: stabilization confirmed + post-incident actions and credits

Elena / Tom — final update and closure notes. TL;DR: fenrir3b service has stabilized, root cause identified, and we have short- and long-term remediation planned.

What happened (summary):
- A memory-management regression in the fenrir3b runtime layer caused KV cache retention to grow under long-running sessions, which produced intermittent blocking GC events and queue saturation. That cascade produced elevated 504/503 responses between 2026-11-24T22:30Z and 2026-11-26T23:10Z.

What we did:
- Immediate fallbacks enabled for your account to fenrir-lite-v2 for large requests.
- Targeted rolling restarts and reduced concurrency limits to relieve pressure.
- Canaryed and rolled a micro-patch that adjusts KV eviction and backpressure; rollout completed 2026-11-26T23:47Z UTC.

Evidence of resolution:
- Error rate for fenrir3b for your project dropped from 4.7% -> 0.08% within 3 hours of the rollout.
- No 5xx observed in the last 12 hours; latency percentile graphs have returned to baseline.

Postmortem & long-term actions:
- Root cause: suboptimal KV cache GC heuristics introduced in runtime v2.1.
- Fixes:
  1) Runtime patch (INF-4821) to change KV cache eviction logic (deployed).
  2) Telemetry improvements: added heap-resident alerting and a low-latency queue-depth metric (Qdepth p95) to detect regressions earlier.
  3) Deployment safety: new canary gating for memory regressions and a temporary lower default concurrency for models with long-context usage.

Customer impact & credits:
- We recognize the disruption to Bright Analytics workflows. We're issuing a one-week service credit applied to your December invoice for the period of elevated failures. Your account team will follow up with the exact credit calculation.

Attachments: fenrir3b-rca.pdf (full RCA), allocation-schedule.csv (restart windows + host list).

Follow-up meeting: If you'd like a 30-minute walkthrough of the RCA and long-term mitigations, I'm available Tue/Wed next week; propose a time and we'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks for your patience and for the detailed logs — that materially sped up diagnosis.

— Markus Klein
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
